message.reasoning: We need to answer: earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record. Likely earliest non-Christian references: Josephus (Antiquities 18.3), Tacitus (Annals 15.44), Pliny the Younger (letters). Also maybe the earliest Christian references: the Gospels (written ~70-90 AD). But question: "earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record?" So likely earliest mention outside Christian texts: Josephus (c. 93-94 AD) and Tacitus (c. 116 AD). The earliest is Josephus. Also maybe the earliest Christian mention: the Gospel of Mark (~70 AD). But the question says "from historical record" meaning non-biblical? Might ask earliest reference from historical record. So answer: Josephus's Antiquities of the Jews, Book 18, Chapter 3, around 93-94 AD. Provide details. Also mention that some scholars debate authenticity. Provide context. Also mention other references: Tacitus, Pliny. Provide citations. Provide explanation.
